results.name: Operation ShadowCloud: initial infection and the GitDoor backdoor
results.description: A sophisticated cyber intrusion campaign dubbed Operation ShadowCloud has been identified targeting government entities across Asia and Africa. Adversaries deploy two novel backdoors, GitDoor and GraphDoor, through the legitimate MeshAgent utility. These implants conceal command-and-control communications by leveraging cloud platforms including Microsoft SharePoint, GitHub, and Ably messaging services, effectively evading network detection mechanisms. The modular toolset supports on-demand plug-in downloads and in-memory shellcode injection, enabling capabilities such as keylogging, screen capture, credential theft, and proxy deployment. The operation employs DLL sideloading techniques with legitimate executables to deliver malicious loaders that decrypt and execute encrypted payloads. Multiple GitHub repositories, created since late 2024, serve as infrastructure for data exfiltration and command distribution. results.name: World's Largest Brands Infected With Malware Via Optimizely
results.description: On 16 November 2026, malicious JavaScript was distributed to 178 organizations through the Optimizely Web experimentation platform, affecting major sites including Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, and HSBC. The multi-purpose malware swapped cryptocurrency wallet addresses, skimmed payment cards, stole cookies and screenshots, and deployed Coruna and DarkSword iOS exploit kits targeting iPhones and iPads. Attackers injected their code into customer Project JavaScript fields within Optimizely snippets, which were then served from trusted cdn.optimizely.com domains. Verified cryptocurrency theft totaling approximately $7,040 occurred within nine hours, with funds moved to exchanges. The payload was rebuilt 26 times throughout the day, adding features including card skimming capabilities. Most malicious code was removed by 21:52 UTC, though Content Security Policy protections could have prevented the attack on properly configured sites.

results.name: XaocMail ClickFix Campaign Drops Phantom53 and HavoX Across Latin America, Asia, and Europe
results.description: A Russian-speaking threat actor operates a sophisticated multi-stage campaign utilizing XaocMail phishing platform, Phantom53 DNS-over-HTTPS command-and-control framework, and Havoc post-exploitation toolkit. The operation leverages Cloudflare Workers infrastructure and ClickFix social engineering lures to deliver malicious MSI payloads. Phantom53 implements stealthy beaconing through public DNS-over-HTTPS resolvers, employs a week-keyed SHA256 domain generation algorithm for resilience, and uses scheduled tasks with Python virtual environments for persistence. The campaign shows evidence of AI-assisted development using Claude Code for automated testing and rapid iteration. Targets span Latin America, particularly Brazil and Peru, followed by entities in Asia and Europe across technology, finance, education, government, logistics, and manufacturing sectors. results.name: Lotuslite V2: The Evolution of Mustang Panda's .NET Backdoor
results.description: This analysis identifies Lotuslite V2 as a .NET successor to LOTUSLITE malware, attributed to Mustang Panda (Earth Preta). The campaign targets Thailand through a public Zoho WorkDrive link delivering an assessment-themed ZIP archive. The infection chain leverages a signed PDFgear executable for DLL side-loading, establishes registry persistence, and initiates TCP connections to command-and-control infrastructure. The evolved variant introduces the PRO1 protocol marker (0x50524F31) and implements application-layer AES-256-GCM encryption. Key modifications include a transition from C++ to managed .NET/C# architecture, enhanced cryptographic protection beyond transport-layer security, and refined command routing through bitwise MSB masking. The operational tradecraft maintains consistency with previous Mustang Panda campaigns, including signed binary abuse, ProgramData staging directories, and registry-based persistence mechanisms targeting government and diplomatic entities in the ASEAN region.

results.name: Detected Exploitation of CVE-2026-90436 against Atlassian Confluence Data Center, N-able N-central also Exploited
results.description: On November 6, 2026, the Apache Software Foundation disclosed CVE-2026-90436, a critical unsafe reflection vulnerability in Apache Axis 1.x that enables unauthenticated remote code execution. The vulnerability affects certain versions of Atlassian Confluence Data Center and N-able N-central when configured with non-default settings. Active exploitation in the wild was detected on November 13, 2026, targeting both products. Affected Confluence versions range from 1.x through 9.x when Remote API is enabled, while N-central requires Legacy API to be active for exploitation. Apache Axis 1.x has reached end of life with no official patches planned. Organizations must apply emergency patches or disable vulnerable APIs immediately, prioritizing internet-accessible instances and investigating exposed systems for compromise indicators.

results.name: Fake Prime Gaming x FC 27 reward site harvests EA passwords and 2FA codes
results.description: Football fans seeking free player packs for EA SPORTS FC 27 are targeted by a sophisticated phishing campaign mimicking Prime Gaming reward pages. The fake site, styled as an official promotion, directs victims to a fraudulent EA sign-in page that captures email addresses, passwords, and two-factor authentication codes. The stolen credentials are sent to attacker-controlled servers that validate entries before proceeding, potentially allowing immediate account takeover. The phishing kit includes tracking capabilities for social media traffic sources and masquerades as an internal authentication tool. Compromised EA accounts may contain valuable virtual assets, purchased games, and payment information. The operation demonstrates advanced credential harvesting techniques specifically targeting the gaming community following FC 27's September launch.

results.name: Typosquatters Copy Big Brands' New Domains Within a Day of Registration
results.description: An ongoing typosquatting campaign has been targeting clients of brand-protection registrars CSC and MarkMonitor by monitoring their new domain registrations. Malicious actors registered 25 lookalike domains using one-character modifications within 24 hours of authentic domains being registered. The campaign targeted major brands including Abbott Laboratories, Bayer, CarMax, McDonald's, Procter & Gamble, and Sanofi. Most authentic domains were designed for marketing campaigns like patient-savings programs, sweepstakes, and legal settlements. The lookalike domains served parked pages, deceptive search portals, and brand-themed blogs containing advertisements routing visitors to scam sites. Registration occurred through China-based registrars Cloud Yuqu LLC and Chengdu West Dimension Digital Technology. Activity continues with new lookalikes detected as recently as November 11, 2026.

results.name: CVE-2026-84869 in ScreenConnect Exploited to Run Malicious Files on MSP Technician Accounts
results.description: A critical vulnerability in ConnectWise ScreenConnect (CVE-2026-84869, CVSS 9.9) allows malicious guests in remote sessions to push files to technician workstations and execute them with elevated privileges without authorization. Between October and November 2026, attackers conducted a massive spray campaign across 42 MSP ScreenConnect servers, issuing 688,000 malicious file-transfer requests. One successful exploitation achieved full compromise in nine seconds, deploying a rogue ScreenConnect client branded as Windows Update and connected to attacker infrastructure at masterdarky[.]com. Attack techniques included worm-like propagation, path traversal to inject startup scripts, and strategic targeting of MSP technician workstations that hold RMM consoles and customer credentials. Additional campaigns planted unauthorized crypto-exchange-named guest sessions as lures, while test runs used canary files to verify exploitation success before deploying actual payloads.

results.name: High volume phishing campaign uses Microsoft 365 outage lures to target multiple industry sectors
results.description: On November 13, 2026, a coordinated high-volume phishing campaign targeted organizations worldwide across multiple sectors. Threat actors disguised emails as legitimate Microsoft 365 service-health notifications, claiming emails were held during a service disruption and would be deleted within 24 hours unless recipients took action. The campaign used specific sender domains including moments-notice[.]com, planetmaison[.]com, and newbooker[.]com, with randomized outage subjects and recipient-specific tracking links leading to reallifeaccounting[.]com. The activity was assessed as credential phishing, though no credential capture, malware delivery, or post-compromise activity was directly observed. Microsoft Defender blocks malicious domains used in this campaign, and Defender for Office 365 quarantines phishing emails.

results.name: QUIC and Covert: Novel HTTP/3-Powered RATs Target Southeast Asian Governments
results.description: A sophisticated multi-stage cyberespionage campaign has been targeting Southeast Asian government entities since July 2025. The activity features two previously undocumented custom remote access Trojans: PerfectPioneer RAT and its successor KUKURAT. These tools demonstrate advanced capabilities including covert HTTP/3 over UDP for command and control communications that bypass traditional TCP-based detection, an operational safety mechanism preventing operators from executing forensics-heavy commands, and multi-vector heuristic camouflage generating synthetic benign activity to obscure malicious operations. The attackers leverage server exploitation and phishing for initial access, manipulate domain log-on scripts for lateral movement, harvest credentials through LSASS dumping and DCSync attacks, and exfiltrate sensitive documents and emails.
